title: Microsoft Dataverse: agent users with a Microsoft Entra agent identity
summary: The briefing needs corrections to its default-state and creation-permission guidance. The roadmap explicitly says the capability is enabled automatically, while Graph requires both an appropriate permission and a supported administrator role for delegated creation, not either one alone.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes agents performing tasks autonomously or on behalf of users.

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No API is documented specifically for adding these agent users to Dataverse environments and assigning their security role.
claims.quote: Searched: add agent user Dataverse environment API PowerShell pac admin security role assign; Dataverse agent user API add. Read create-users, agent-users, pac admin assign-user excerpts; searched systemuser reference for agentuser and agentidentity. No agent-user provisioning API found.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/microsoft.graph.agentUser creates an Entra agent user.
claims.quote:
Create a new agentUser object.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users/microsoft.graph.agentUser

claims.claim: The creation request's identityParentId property specifies the associated agent identity's object ID.
claims.quote: identityParentId | String | The object ID of the associated agent identity. Required.

claims.claim: The Graph reference names Agent ID Administrator as the least privileged supported role for agent-user creation.
claims.quote: For delegated access using work or school accounts, the admin must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role ... Agent ID Administrator is the least privileged role supported for this operation.

claims.claim: No Microsoft Entra admin center creation steps are documented for linking an agent user account to an agent identity.
claims.quote: Searched: create agent user account Microsoft Entra admin center UI steps. Read create-delete-agent-user-account and agent-id-creation-channels: creation procedure uses Graph; portal steps grant blueprint permissions, while creation channels lists roles without a portal route.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The default state is unknown because Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival.
claims.quote: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically
claims.fix: Set defaultState to "on". Replace the sentence ending "Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival" with "The roadmap says the capability is enabled for admins, makers and marketers automatically; Learn separately documents how an administrator adds an individual agent user." Replace the corresponding arrival question with "Does enabling the capability automatically provision any Dataverse agent users?" In the risk rationale, replace "the roadmap's default wording differs from Learn's procedure" with "the roadmap describes automatic availability while Learn documents per-agent setup". Automatic capability availability and individual account provisioning are different facts.

claims.claim: The sources do not state that this change modifies existing users, apps or agents.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent users enabled automatically existing users agents default; Dataverse agent users Entra Agent ID tenant switch default enabled automatically. Read roadmap, create-users agent sections and agent-users. No migration or existing-user/app change stated.

claims.claim: A user's presence in an environment does not itself grant Dataverse data access.
claims.quote: A user's presence in an environment doesn't grant access to Dataverse data.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No dedicated Dataverse agent-user meter is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent users Entra agent identity licensing price meter; Dataverse agent users licensing price. Read agent-users, create-users agent sections and pricing-billing-skus. General Power Platform meters exist, but no dedicated agent-user meter was specified.

claims.claim: No feature-specific price is published for Dataverse agent users.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent users licensing price; Dataverse agent users Entra agent identity licensing price meter. Read feature pages and Power Platform licensing overview; Entra licensing links Agent 365 pricing but states no Dataverse agent-user price.

claims.claim: The sources do not state that a Dataverse agent user, simply by being added, requires Microsoft Agent 365.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent user Agent 365 license requirement. Read agent-users, create-users agent sections, Entra licensing and agent-users account overview. Agent 365 requirements describe Microsoft 365 participation and extended security, not Dataverse agent-user addition alone.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[2].note; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited agent-user pages and Entra monitoring page do not describe Dataverse auditing behaviour for these agent users.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent users auditing actions audit logs security role limits autonomous on behalf user. Read agent-users, create-users agent sections and manage-agent-identities-admin; general Dataverse auditing search results do not add agent-specific behaviour to those pages.

claims.claim: The Dataverse agent-user procedure does not state an automatic restriction on the security role an administrator can select.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent user role autonomous delegated behalf security roles limits. Read create-users agent procedure and agent-users: administrator selects a security role; no agent-specific role cap is stated.

claims.claim: Learn's Dataverse agent-user steps do not explain how the assigned role operates separately in autonomous and on-behalf-of-user modes.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse agent user role autonomous delegated behalf security roles limits. Read create-users agent procedure and agent-users. Neither gives mode-specific Dataverse role evaluation; Entra agent-users distinguishes user-delegated access from the agent's own user account.

claims.claim: The cited Dataverse agent-user pages do not name the role required to add agents in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse add agent user Power Platform admin center required role System Administrator; Dataverse agent users role admin. Read create-users agent procedure and agent-users. General admin-role results exist, but these pages specify no role for this operation.

claims.claim: An Entra agent's user account cannot have credentials such as passwords or passkeys.
claims.quote: The agent's user account can't have credentials like passwords or passkeys. The only credential type it supports is the agent identity reference to its parent.

claims.claim: Authentication of the agent user account is controlled through its parent agent identity.
claims.quote: Can only authenticate by presenting a token issued to the associated agent identity.

claims.claim: Creating an Entra agent user needs either the Agent ID Administrator role or the AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.IdentityParentedBy permission.
claims.quote: Delegated (work or school account) | AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.IdentityParentedBy ... For delegated access using work or school accounts, the admin must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role
claims.fix: Replace the creation-permission sentence with "For delegated creation, the Graph reference lists AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.IdentityParentedBy as the least privileged permission and additionally requires a supported administrator role, with Agent ID Administrator the least privileged. For application access, it lists AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.IdentityParentedBy as the least privileged application permission." These are the requirements at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/agentuser-post; the role is not a substitute for an API permission.
